title: The Pudding
why: Visual essays that answer odd questions with data, such as how song lyrics have changed.

title: Dear Data
why: Two designers sent each other hand-drawn charts of their week on postcards for a year.

title: Spurious correlations
why: Charts of things that track each other perfectly and have nothing to do with each other.

title: Benford's law
why: In many real data sets about 30% of numbers start with 1. Auditors use this to spot fraud.

title: Citizen science
why: Zooniverse lets you classify galaxies, count penguins or transcribe old ship logs for real research.

title: Florence Nightingale's diagrams
why: She used a new kind of chart to persuade the British government that hospitals were killing soldiers.

title: John Snow's cholera map
why: Dots on a street map of London pointed to one water pump and changed public health.

title: Minard's map
why: Napoleon's march on Moscow drawn in 1869 as a single shrinking line. Often called the best chart ever made.

title: Anscombe's quartet
why: Four data sets with the same averages and correlations that look nothing alike when plotted.

title: Simpson's paradox
why: A trend that holds in every group can reverse when the groups are added together.

title: Our World in Data
why: Long-run charts on almost everything, from child mortality to the price of light.

title: Dollar Street
why: Photos of homes around the world, sorted by income. People at the same income live alike everywhere.

title: Survivorship bias
why: The wartime story of the bombers that came back, and why the armour belonged where they had no holes.

title: Seeing Theory
why: A visual introduction to probability where every idea is something you can drag and play with.

title: The birthday problem
why: In a room of 23 people there is an even chance that two share a birthday.

title: Zipf's law
why: In any language the second most common word appears about half as often as the first. Nobody is sure why.

title: OpenStreetMap
why: A map of the whole world drawn by volunteers, and free for anyone to download as data.

title: W. E. B. Du Bois's charts
why: Hand-drawn, strikingly modern charts on Black life in America, made for the 1900 Paris Exposition.

title: Sonification
why: Turning data into sound in place of pictures. A Geiger counter is the everyday example.

title: The wisdom of crowds
why: At a 1906 fair, the middle guess of the crowd for the weight of an ox was almost exactly right.
